summary: Interpreted the fourth receipt (20c7c72772474093bd6093a37b84448f, exit 0, both cases passed): all six boundary comparisons are complete and hold, so the two limits the account still stated are resolved. The monotonic-store case stalls exactly like the non-monotonic one — restores 5 -> 1102 in 3s, applied index fixed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, cached claim persisting — and its install branch emptied the log store (first and last index 0, no suffix kept at probe index 14), which shows the surviving on-disk suffix is not required and narrows the cause to the cached claim outranking the installed snapshot. The repair case (probe index 33) first records the stall, then drives the leader past the follower's claim of 97, publishes a snapshot at 98, and the follower resumes: applied 83 -> 109 equal to the frontier, commit 109, claim repaired — confirming that the starvation lasts while the newest snapshot index stays at or below the claim. This turn therefore records the settled account (conclusion explained, defect_claim asserted, citing all four receipts), drops the two resolved limits from the account, adds the source-reasoned safety reading that requestVote uses the same phantom claim for its own log, states the minority bound it relies on together with the configuration-change caveat, and registers a child investigation @q_phantom_claim_vote_decision whose discriminator is a five-voter history in which the same RequestVote is delivered to a phantom holder and to a consistent voter (grant plus rejection would establish the changed decision; equal outcomes would refute it). No experiment was requested this turn, so the vote probe, a production BoltDB-style monotonic store, larger clusters and longer windows remain unmeasured.
